highlights.label: daily users served on a SaaS platform I built

paragraphs: I'm a software engineer who likes the parts of the job most people avoid: schema decisions that decide how a product behaves two years later, auth flows that have to be airtight, and pipelines that can't drop a record. Over two years across three companies, I've built modular SaaS platforms serving over a thousand daily users, shipped a full backend from zero to production in under six months, and tuned .NET APIs down from 500ms to 250ms.

Right now I'm doing my Master's in Computer Science at Northeastern in Boston, where I've also worked as a teaching assistant for the graduate Database Systems course. My interests sit at the intersection of backend systems and applied AI — most recently a knowledge-graph-augmented RAG pipeline over the Mahabharata, and a multi-objective portfolio optimizer implementing NSGA-II from scratch.
I care about building things that are correct under load, failure, and scale — not just things that demo well.
